key_idea: Find three different numbers, each 2 or more, that add up to 9.
steps: Start as small as possible: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9. That is exactly 9.
Any other set of three different numbers, each 2 or more, adds up to more than 9.
Nora has 2, the least. Mila has 4, the most.

choice_feedback.A: Nora has the least, so Otto has more than Nora. Otto cannot have just 2.
choice_feedback.B: 4 is the most nuts anyone has, and Mila has the most.
choice_feedback.C: If Otto had 5, the other two would share 4 nuts, so they would both have 2. They must all have different numbers.
choice_feedback.E: Each squirrel has at least 2 nuts, so nobody has 1.
